definitions.explanation: A favorable point or benefit of something. Used when discussing the positive aspects of a choice, method, or situation.

examples.japanese: この{方法|ほうほう}の{利点|りてん}は{何|なん}ですか。
examples.english: What are the advantages of this method?

examples.japanese: {都会|とかい}に{住|す}む{利点|りてん}は{交通|こうつう}の{便|べん}が{良|よ}いことだ。
examples.english: The advantage of living in the city is the good transportation access.

examples.japanese: この{製品|せいひん}には{多|おお}くの{利点|りてん}があるが、{価格|かかく}が{高|たか}いという{欠点|けってん}もある。
examples.english: This product has many merits, but it also has the drawback of being expensive.

notes:
{利点|りてん} means a favorable point or benefit. Often used in analytical or comparative contexts, such as weighing options.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {利点|りてん}がある: to have an advantage
- {最大|さいだい}の{利点|りてん}: the greatest advantage
- {利点|りてん}と{欠点|けってん}: advantages and disadvantages
- {利点|りてん}を{生|い}かす: to make the most of an advantage

SIMILAR WORDS:
- メリット: merit, advantage (loanword, very common in casual speech)
- {長所|ちょうしょ}: strong point (often about people)
- {強|つよ}み: strength (personal or organizational)

CONTRAST:
- {欠点|けってん}: drawback, flaw
- デメリット: disadvantage, demerit
- {短所|たんしょ}: weak point
